final_proposal.thesis: This portfolio balances the retired surgeon’s need for growth with strict risk management by anchoring 30% in legacy JNJ, then allocating the remaining 70% to three high-conviction sectors: Technology (MSFT) for growth, Consumer Staples (PG) for volatility control, and Financials (JPM, GS) for value and diversification. We exclude all fossil fuels, high-volatility tech names (NVDA, META, GOOGL, AMZN), and additional healthcare (UNH) to stay within the 18% volatility cap, the 35% single-position/sector limits, and the 8-holding maximum, effectively replacing the drag of TLT and KO with more efficient growth and stability drivers. (Note: dropped TGT, not in this client's universe.)

reasons.GS: Included as a selective financial holding offering strong value and growth with manageable correlation, fitting within the diversification needs.
reasons.JNJ: Included at 30% to satisfy the mandatory legacy holding requirement and tax constraints, serving as the core defensive anchor.
reasons.JPM: Included as the preferred financial position over GS or BAC due to its lower volatility and better risk-adjusted returns, providing stable growth.
reasons.MSFT: Included as the primary growth engine, offering strong fundamentals, momentum, and a more manageable risk profile compared to other tech peers.
reasons.PG: Included to provide essential stability and downside protection, balancing the growth exposure from Tech and Financials while keeping volatility in check.
